answers.puzzle_1_rating_reason: Doesn't feel like its solvable with "trivial" logic (i.e. freebees, using other solved rows/columns), had to consider multiple columns at once, or the effects of setting on square.
answers.puzzle_2_rating_reason: Didn't have to guess at all, however the "early game" had less free squares to work with.
answers.puzzle_3_rating_reason: Got stuck at two points and had to use a hint, due to earlier mistakes. It seems like there are times where you just have to guess or see what happens when making a move, you can't always use logical deduction to solve it.
answers.strategy: Look for "free columns" (every piece is known given the numbers and gaps), If the general location of a line is known, filling in squares that have to be black/white based on that. Looking at remaining parts of columns to fill in white/X squares.
answers.comments: Easier could generally be solved by only looking at one row/column at a time. Harder ones required you to look at multiple rows/columns at once in order to deduce information without guessing.
